answer.rationale: The 18% spend mandate and the low-cost vendor's competitive quote create a cost imperative. memory_c2 shows the low-cost vendor has proven onboarding speed and invoicing accuracy in prior deployment. memory_c4 demonstrates that negotiation recovers margin but is time-constrained—with 14 days to renewal and no auto-renewal clause, renegotiation carries execution risk. The assembly line at 94% utilization presents delivery risk if the switch encounters friction. However, memory_c2's track record of quick integration and memory_c6's insight that longer-term commitments unlock volume pricing suggest a structured multi-year contract with the low-cost vendor can simultaneously meet the mandate and stabilize supply. This decision consumes the single sourcing cycle available; other measures wait for next review. Flagging that 94% utilization leaves minimal buffer—any onboarding delay compounds risk.
